guide.summary: Internal tool inside your Workspace org (approval path unconfirmed); Public app, sensitive scopes only (approval path unconfirmed); Public app, restricted scopes on your servers (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed Gmail app, fine for prototypes. For launch, create a custom auth config with your own Google client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, no: Composio's managed Gmail app works. For production you should use your own app so users see your brand, and so you get your own quota and scopes.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Composio's default scopes may not cover what you need
Custom auth config allows your own scopes and rate limits

prerequisites.title: Verified domain and public home page
prerequisites.detail: Verify your authorized domains in Google Search Console. Your home page must be publicly accessible.

prerequisites.title: Accurate consent screen branding
prerequisites.detail: App name, support email, home page and privacy policy must represent the app's identity.

prerequisites.title: Google Workspace organization
prerequisites.detail: Internal use requires users to be in your Workspace or Cloud Identity organization.

steps.title: Create project and configure consent screen
steps.detail: In the Google API Console open Google Auth platform, set app info, support email and user type, and agree to the user data policy.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list
steps.detail: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes for your features and look for non-sensitive alternatives to sensitive or restricted ones.

steps.title: Create OAuth client with Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Create a web OAuth client in Google and paste the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard. Keep the client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Gmail auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Verify domain and publish pages
steps.detail: Verify domain ownership in Search Console and publish a public home page and privacy policy.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and demo script
steps.detail: Write per-scope justifications and a demo script that shows exactly the scopes configured in the console.

steps.title: Record demo and submit verification
steps.detail: Record the demo, provide working test credentials, publish branding, and submit for verification.

steps.title: Wait for brand verification
steps.detail: Brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days if branding changed since the last approval.

steps.title: Wait for scope verification
steps.detail: Check the verification centre manually, since rejection emails may not arrive.

steps.title: Complete security assessment
steps.detail: Engage an assessor, fix findings and get sign-off. Reported at 4-6 weeks.

steps.title: Ask org admin to allowlist app
steps.detail: If your admin restricts third-party apps, have them allow the app.
steps.done_when: Users in your org can connect.

traps.title: Rejections can arrive silently
traps.detail: One developer saw 10+ rejections over about two months without emails. Common causes were scope justification length, demo scopes not matching console scopes, and missing test credentials.

traps.title: Restricted scopes need a security assessment
traps.detail: If restricted data passes through a third-party server, a Google-empanelled assessor must review the app.

traps.title: Unverified apps are capped at 100 users
traps.detail: Apps with sensitive or restricted scopes show an unverified warning and are capped at 100 total users.

traps.title: Testing mode limits
traps.detail: External apps in Testing allow only 100 allowlisted test users, and refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

traps.title: Consent screen cannot be removed
traps.detail: Once configured, the consent screen cannot be removed, so use the right project.

traps.title: Managed app shares quota
traps.detail: Composio's managed app shares quota across all Composio users.

blockers.what_it_means: Your app exceeded Google's new user authorization rate limit.
blockers.what_to_do: Request a rate limit quota increase; Google says to expect a response in 5 business days.

blockers.what_it_means: The app has not completed verification and must submit a verification request.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare scope justifications and demo script.

blockers.symptom: Workspace users cannot authorize the app
blockers.what_it_means: Their admin may have blocked it or may require an allowlist. Verified status does not override admin settings.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's admin to allow the app.

open_questions: Which Gmail scopes are sensitive and which are restricted? The scope-classification page was not found; check the Gmail scopes table in the Google docs.
Does Google require redirect-URI domain verification for the Composio callback? Not found; test in the Google Cloud console or ask Composio support.
What does the security assessment cost and which assessors are available? Not found; check Google's app assessment (CASA) page.
Are there verification-time numbers from Google itself? Only reported figures were found; ask Google verification support.
